changes.problem: Benchmark outputs repeatedly introduced unsupported facts or slightly expanded source requirements, including plausible physical parameters and interface behavior.
changes.change: Added explicit evidence classification, source-location tracking, bidirectional validation, and prohibitions on inferred, calculated, customary, sample-derived, or externally remembered facts.
changes.reason: This generalizes the recurring source-fidelity failure without encoding any benchmark-specific value or solution.

changes.problem: Some supplied administrative facts were replaced by unresolved placeholders, while other absent administrative details were filled ambiguously.
changes.change: Required exact preservation of supplied names, performers, designations, and administrative facts, while limiting blanks and unresolved markers to genuinely missing fields that belong in scope.
changes.reason: The distinction prevents both omission of known facts and fabrication of unknown metadata.

changes.problem: Generated documents sometimes added auxiliary sections or inconsistently formatted title, approval, signature, and table elements.
changes.change: Introduced provision-level applicability mapping and clarified that structural elements must be requested or mandated, with prescribed organization applied consistently when mandatory.
changes.reason: This improves GOST structure compliance while preserving the user's requested document scope.

changes.problem: Normative references, official expansions, and source terminology were occasionally omitted, generalized, or inaccurately restated.
changes.change: Added rules to inventory and preserve normative references, official designations, source-provided abbreviation expansions, and terminology without memory-based correction.
changes.reason: These details are material source facts and require the same fidelity controls as numeric requirements.

changes.problem: Verification coverage was often present but some methods, tolerances, recovery criteria, and measurable pass conditions remained incomplete or were expanded beyond the evidence.
changes.change: Defined a coverage tuple of condition, action, observable result, source-supported criterion, and method, and required precise gap identification whenever a complete method cannot be supported.
changes.reason: This raises verification completeness without encouraging invented thresholds or procedures.

changes.problem: Related requirements were sometimes generalized, repeated, or expressed with reduced precision across architecture, interfaces, synchronization, diagnostics, and failure handling.
changes.change: Strengthened preservation of ownership, directionality, quantities, mode transitions, alarm propagation, recovery behavior, and logical grouping, with one authoritative location per requirement.
changes.reason: This improves technical clarity and traceability while avoiding divergent restatements.

changes.problem: Final review focused mainly on whether source requirements appeared, leaving unsupported document statements less systematically detected.
changes.change: Required both source-to-document completeness review and document-to-source support review after reopening the generated artifact.
changes.reason: The two-way check catches omissions as well as hallucinated additions.
